name: Heartland AI Campus
subtitle: Strathcona County · 100 MW IT · phased gas-backed development
verdict: Base economics fail the hurdle; advance only bounded diligence, no investment decision
thesis: Develop four 25 MW liquid-cooled halls on a marketed Heartland tract, pairing 100 MW IT with 160 MW net modular gas generation and a conditional transmission connection. Sell committed powered/cooled capacity; earn the right to build each next phase through land, service, permits and tenant evidence.
executiveSummary: A real 160-acre candidate gives the concept a testable land basis. Its AG zoning, estimated fibre and nearby transmission are unresolved development work, not proof of site readiness.
Alberta’s initial large-load allocation is fully assigned. A new project must prove a final BYOG route, acceptable net-load behavior and gas deliverability before it can promise service.
The owner develops facility and power assets; customers own GPUs and cloud revenue. All underwriting is native CAD and electricity operating costs are passed through separately from capacity rent.

The base schedule assumes first 25 MW at project month 42 and 100 MW at month 69, with each phase conditioned on contracts and approvals. No utility, landowner, vendor, lender or customer has committed.

At the current assumptions the monthly model has negative NPV at the 15% hurdle; approve only bounded diligence to test whether achievable rent, cost and delivery terms can support a revised case. No investment decision is supported.

site.name: Sandhills Heartland candidate — SE 23-56-21-W4
site.addressOrArea: Township Road 564 and Range Road 211; legal description SE 23-56-21-W4
site.coordinateBasis: Exact public listing HTML map marker; an approximate location pin, not surveyed parcel boundaries.
site.landStatus: Publicly marketed 160-acre tract; availability, beneficial ownership, asking price and control unconfirmed. No option, contact or access right.
site.rationale: An identified large tract within the Sandhills Heavy Industrial Policy Area offers a concrete screening target for co-located power and four halls. Nearby transmission and industrial transport warrant diligence, while AG zoning and uncertain services prevent a readiness claim.
constraints: AG zoning at listing; industrial policy area does not confer development permission.
Nearby 240 kV line is only geographic evidence; capacity, tap rights, route and costs unknown.
Fibre ready/available flag is explicitly estimated; two routes and latency unverified.
Coronado Gas Co-op franchise proximity does not establish industrial gas deliverability.
Survey, wetlands, geotechnics, contamination, flood/industrial hazard contours and receptor setbacks unresolved.

Concept drawings use a 600 m x 800 m / 48 ha campus plus an adjoining 187.5 m x 800 m / 15 ha generation zone (787.5 m x 800 m, 63 ha gross) within a 64.75 ha tract; not a cadastral fit or buildable-area finding.

alternatives.name: 55021 Range Road 225, Sturgeon County
alternatives.reason: Actual 73.23-acre industrial listing with I4 zoning; brochure says only roughly 20 acres remain for lease. Existing gas/power services have no proven 100 MW capacity.
alternatives.decision: Reject as base for co-located 100 MW + generation: available lease area too small without additional control. Retain only for smaller phase or off-site-power alternative.

alternatives.name: Edmonton Energy and Technology Park
alternatives.reason: City describes an existing chemical-cluster route for major data-centre/utility uses; medium-industrial inclusion is a live amendment, not approved. No controlled offering identified here.
alternatives.decision: Retain as relocation alternative if a large chemical-cluster tract and utilities can be secured; do not rely on proposed zoning changes.

power.strategy: Conditional BYOG: 160 MW net-at-site modular gas generation paired with a transmission-connected 100 MW IT campus; prefer approved island-capable design, with grid import/export limits set only by studies and agreements.
power.gridRoute: Investigate AltaLink 943L / 1054L corridor reported 1.35 km from listing; 4 x 50 MVA, 240/34.5 kV concept station. Exact connection point, circuits, redundancy and easements unselected; no right to connect.
power.generationRoute: 16 x 10 MW net procurement target, installed 6/9/13/16 by phase; 160 MW ultimate and 140 MW with two modules unavailable. Generation CAPEX uses cost-weighted shares of approximately 47.0486% / 15.8854% / 21.1806% / 15.8854%: all CAD55m of shared gas-lateral/BESS cost is in phase 1, with remaining CAD305m allocated by 6 / 3 / 4 / 3 added modules. Remaining BOP/civils proportional allocation is approximate; actual deposits are not modeled. Add 25 MW / 25 MWh plant BESS for dynamics and independent emergency facility supply; vendor-guaranteed site performance required.
power.utility: AESO connection/system access; prospective transmission owner AltaLink based on nearby assets. Gas provider and firm upstream service unconfirmed; local franchise listing is not a supply offer.
constraints: No share of Phase 1 allocation and no final BYOG qualification confirmed.
Generation-to-load ratio, tethering, export treatment, curtailment and bridging load require current process confirmation.
125 MW site peak envelope differs from 100 MW IT; annual PUE 1.20 is not a grid sizing guarantee.
Off-grid operation is a separate permitted/customer-approved scenario, not an automatic bypass.
All-electric grid-only alternative rejected as base for lack of allocated capacity; remote-generation PPA retained if a partner can offer an eligible, financeable route.
No merchant export, ancillary-service or heat-sale income underwritten.

cooling.strategy: Direct-to-chip liquid cooling with isolated facility water/glycol loops, N+1 pumping/CDUs, dry outdoor heat rejection and mechanical trim. Reserve residual room cooling for network/air-cooled loads; validate customer temperature class before equipment selection.
cooling.climateImplications: Cold climate supports economizer operation but requires glycol isolation, freeze protection, snow/ice access, cold-start controls and smoke filtration. Annual PUE 1.20; +35 C primary / +40 C stress and -40 C winter checks are assumptions pending site weather modelling.
cooling.waterStrategy: No routine evaporative campus or engine cooling in base. Positive domestic, maintenance, initial-fill and fire requirements remain; assume 50 m3/day service allowance and independently size fire storage. Do not claim zero water or a water licence.

commercial.customer: One creditworthy Canadian or international AI/cloud operator taking the initial 25 MW, with later 25 MW blocks reserved under separately funded expansion rights; no prospect is named or represented as interested.
commercial.offering: Wholesale dedicated powered/cooled IT capacity in 5 MW suites within 25 MW buildings; customer procures/runs GPUs, network and software. Landlord provides facility, utility interface, cooling, security and operations.
commercial.contracting: Target 10–15 year take-or-pay lease with capacity rent, annual indexation, metered power operating-cost pass-through, reserved capacity charges, explicit carbon/tax allocation, technical interface schedule, agreed curtailment envelope, commissioning acceptance, service credits and capped delay liabilities. Credit support via parent guarantee or LC. No SLA promising grid independence until proven. The 20-year model includes a 5-year initial-phase tail beyond a 15-year lease (longer beyond 10 years), with no renewal discount or downtime; renewal/reletting is uncontracted risk, not committed revenue.
commercial.financing: Single sponsor holding facility and generation SPVs with enforceable service, easement and intercreditor arrangements; consolidated model includes generation CAPEX so transfer pricing cannot create artificial returns. Target 55% senior debt at 7.5%, 20-year amortization; equity funds early diligence and contingent commitments. No subsidies, tax-credit proceeds, GPU sales or merchant exports in base.
goToMarket: Prepare a technical data room with constraint map, three power cases and the full cost boundary.
Qualify anchor credit and Canadian data-residency needs; test willingness to accept gas emissions and AESO curtailment terms.
Obtain conditional 25 MW lease and price later blocks as options with paid reservation deadlines.
Seek generation/EPC and institutional infrastructure partners against the defined risk allocation.
Release later phases only when booked capacity, funding, service and commissioning evidence support them.
counterpartyQuestions: Will an anchor sign CAD235/kW-month plus metered energy, with credit support and a credible delivery range?
What inlet temperatures, peak load steps, density, power-quality ride-through and maintenance windows must be guaranteed?
Which party is legally liable for the 2026 computing-equipment levy, and can the lease recover it without relying on tax-credit realization?
Will AESO accept the paired generator configuration, net import limit, dynamic behavior and phase sequence?
Can firm gas supply survive cold-day pressure and upstream outages, and who pays for dedicated infrastructure?
Will lenders finance co-located generation and tenant lease together at the modeled leverage and tenor?

risks.mitigation: 25 MW take-or-pay with credit security; later phases only against signed expansion commitments

risks.risk: Fibre availability is estimated, routes share failure points

assumptions.label: Delivered gas price

assumptions.label: Gas delivery reservation
assumptions.basis: Approximate peak reservation at 160 MW and 7.6 GJ/MWh using 38 MJ/m3; specification requires actual gas assay.

assumptions.label: Ramp / island support BESS
assumptions.basis: 25 MW / 25 MWh plant-side concept; does not replace full-campus UPS or stand-alone reliability study.

assumptions.label: Delivered operating energy allowance
assumptions.basis: Fuel 41.8 + plant variable service 17 + emissions reserve 25 + residual grid/transport balancing 21.2 + operations reserve 15 = 120; capital recovery is in rent, not here.

assumptions.label: Facility hard cost
assumptions.basis: Independent total screening allowance allocated as shell/fit-out 2430, electrical/UPS/standby 5400, cooling/CDUs 2970, civil/drainage 1350, controls/security/fibre 675, testing/commissioning 675; excludes land/grid/gas plant/soft/contingency.

assumptions.label: Land acquisition allowance
assumptions.basis: About CAD50,000/acre for marketed tract, placeholder; not asking price or appraisal.

assumptions.label: Grid interface allowance
assumptions.basis: Off-plot line/routing, easements, grid reinforcement contribution, utility studies and interface works only; receiving station is included in facility electrical CAPEX; no utility estimate.

assumptions.label: Gas plant and BESS allowance
assumptions.basis: CAD2,250/kW of 160 MW net: engine packages 175m, generation BOP 85m, gas lateral 25m, BESS 30m, dedicated civils/electrical 45m. Shared lateral+BESS 55m is fully phase 1; remaining 305m allocated by incremental 6/3/4/3 engines. Proportional BOP/civils is approximate; deposits not modeled; no vendor bids.

assumptions.label: Soft costs
assumptions.basis: Engineering, owner development, permitting, legal, management; financing costs follow model convention separately.

assumptions.label: Contingency
assumptions.unit: percent of hard plus soft cost
assumptions.basis: Screening reserve; scenarios need -20/+35 percent total cost swing, not a confidence interval.

assumptions.label: Fixed non-energy OPEX
assumptions.basis: Facility/plant staffing 8m, property tax 18m, insurance 4m, fixed plant service 2m, security/admin 3m. Tax allowance approximates 900m non-residential and 400m M&E assessment at published 2026 rates; assessments and premiums unconfirmed.

assumptions.label: Variable non-energy OPEX
assumptions.basis: Facility maintenance, spares, consumables; excludes gas-plant variable service embedded in energy allowance.

assumptions.label: Capacity rent
assumptions.basis: Target underwriting assumption for powered/cooled wholesale facility with generation capital; not a signed rent or market quote.

assumptions.label: Stabilized committed capacity
assumptions.basis: Economic occupancy assumption; unleased capacity is not billed.

assumptions.label: Load on committed IT
assumptions.basis: Tenant metered demand assumption; separated from rent-bearing committed capacity.

assumptions.label: Senior debt share

assumptions.label: Debt interest

assumptions.label: Debt amortization
assumptions.basis: Illustrative term; refinance and maturity structure must be negotiated.

assumptions.label: Equity hurdle

assumptions.label: First block operation

assumptions.label: Outdoor summer check
assumptions.basis: Assumed primary thermal sizing point; check capacity at 40 C stress. Not an ASHRAE/NBC site statistic.

assumptions.label: Outdoor winter check

assumptions.label: Routine cooling evaporation
assumptions.basis: Dry heat rejection for campus and engines; fill, maintenance, domestic and fire water remain positive.

assumptions.label: Domestic/service water planning

assumptions.label: Indicative direct combustion intensity
assumptions.basis: 7.6 GJ/MWh x assumed 50 kg CO2/GJ; excludes upstream emissions and methane slip; not a compliance inventory.

killCriteria: No controllable, developable tract with a defensible consent path by month 6.
No written viable BYOG/grid and firm gas route by month 12; do not fund speculative halls while power remains indeterminate.
No bankable 25 MW anchor commitment by month 12 at terms that pass updated cost and downside underwriting.
Unmitigable noise/air, wetland, industrial-neighbour or emergency-response conflict.
No firm first-phase service path within 54 project months, unless a customer signs a revised economic case.
Updated price/cost/financing case fails the 15% equity screen or downside debt-service requirements; reduce/reshape scope only through a new investment decision.
Customer decarbonization or availability requirements cannot be reconciled with the actual power/fuel design.
nextActions: 1. Verify listing availability, title, zoning map and seller willingness to grant a conditional option; obtain boundary survey and access rights.
